final_message:
I've built the Nocturne landing page, but I couldn't run `npm run build`: there's no Node in this sandbox (`env: node: No such file or directory`). Neither the type check nor the Vite build has run, and nobody has looked at the page in a browser. Run `npm run build` first; I checked the types by reading the code, which isn't proof.

Nobody was available, so both theses and the design system are my proposals and none of them was approved (the pipeline marks them **UNVALIDATED**). The previews were written as standalone pages, as you specified. bunshin (the multi-agent pipeline for whole sites) would not fit: this is one page.

## The page
- **Hero:** the sky above Lisbon at 22:00 on Friday 9 October 2026, drawn from `data/stars.json`. All 403 stars and Saturn, sized by magnitude and tinted by their B–V colour index. Zenith at the centre, horizon at the edge, north up, east left, altitude rings every 30°. It is fully drawn when the page loads.
  - Wide screens: the chart takes the right seven columns; title, times, prices and "Book tickets" sit on the left.
  - Phones: the title first, then the whole chart at full width.
- **The evening:** 21:30 doors, 22:00 first show (the sky with a narrator, then the 40-minute show), 23:30 last show. The times are set large.
- **Tonight's sky:** a chart that stays in view, plus a list of Saturn, Vega, Capella, Altair, Fomalhaut, Deneb and Polaris. Each entry gives altitude, compass direction, magnitude and one note.
  - The notes are worked out from the data (brightness rank, Polaris at 38.8° beside Lisbon's 38.72° N) or taken from its text (Saturn five days after opposition).
  - A closing paragraph, also generated from the data, says what isn't drawn: no Moon (under 1% lit and below the horizon), Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter below the horizon, Uranus and Neptune up but too faint.
- **Practical:** days, doors, shows, tickets (12 EUR, 8 EUR for students), "Book tickets" linking to `/tickets`.
- **Footer:** credits for the Bright Star Catalogue, the IAU star names (the data's licence asks for this credit) and NASA JPL Horizons.
- **Not invented:** the planetarium, an address, constellation lines, reviews or counts. "Book tickets" is the only action label.

## Theses (UNVALIDATED)
- **Visual thesis:**
  - **Look:** an observer's all-sky chart printed in light on night. The background darkens section by section from dusk blue-slate `#1c2735` to near-black `#06080b`. One red, `#ff6a55`, is used only for the pointer, the times and the ticket button.
  - **Type:** system fonts only, since no font request was agreed and there is no network. The sans carries display and body with tabular figures; star names are italic serif, as on star atlases.
  - **Layout:** airy, 8px base, one 12-column grid, 34rem reading width. Sharp, flat, hairline borders, no shadows.
- **Interaction thesis:**
  - Hovers are 160ms ease-out, colour only.
  - Nothing moves on scroll.
  - Forbidden: twinkling, particles, glow, load-in fades, bounce, scaling on hover.
  - **The one motion:** a red pointer ring moves across the chart (420ms, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`) to whichever object you hover, focus or tap. It starts on Saturn. With reduced motion it jumps instead.
- **Allowed patterns:** hairline rules and altitude rings; italic serif labels; tabular figures; the stepped dusk-to-night background; the red pointer ring; small uppercase labels.
- **Set aside:** navy with twinkling particles and nebula glow; white museum page with photos; sci-fi HUD; nebula photography. **Kept:** the observer's all-sky horizon chart.
- **Assumptions taken from the brief:** the audience is adults on a night out; the mood is nocturnal, exact, unhurried; no references were given; system fonts.
- **Design-system lookup:** dials sent were variance 6, motion 2, density 3. I kept its contrast floor, 44px touch targets and test widths. I dropped its waitlist/countdown pattern, light navy palette, Outfit + Work Sans fonts, scroll reveals and glow.

## Audit: 11 checked, 3 problems found, 4 handed over

**What the code shows** (all in `src/App.tsx` / `src/index.css`):
- **First screen:** the hero chart is drawn at rest from data at `App.tsx:32`, with no entrance animation.
- **Width:** the hero text takes columns 1–5 (`index.css:188`), the chart 6–12 (`:232`). The evening times take 5–12 (`:249`), the sky chart 1–6 (`:274`), and the practical facts the full width (`:356`). All share one left edge.
- **Phones** (`index.css:397`): everything goes to one column, the hero chart is full width and whole, and the sky chart sticks to the top at up to 42% of the screen height (`:425`).
- **Empty areas:** none.
- **The one motion:** the ring at `SkyChart.tsx:83`, timed at `index.css:169`; it starts on Saturn (`App.tsx:74`).

**Checks:**
- **Motion matches the thesis:** 160ms, 420ms and both easings are in `tokens.css` and used at `index.css:102/161/170/303/313`. The palette and fonts are all tokens.
- **Reduced motion:** `tokens.css:60` sets both durations to 0ms, so the ring jumps and hovers are instant.
- **Exit animations:** none needed; nothing is removed from the page.
- **No layout-property animation:** only transform, opacity, colour and fill are transitioned.
- **Focus visible:** 2px ink outline on the buttons and list entries (`index.css:110`, `:324`); no outline is removed.
- **Five states:** the button and list entries have default, hover, focus, active and disabled. Hover styles only apply on devices that can hover.
- **Tokens:** every colour and spacing value is a token. The chart's SVG sizes are listed in MASTER.md under chart geometry.
- **Contrast (computed):**

  | Pair | Ratio |
  |---|---|
  | ink `#ece6da` on `#1c2735` | 12.15:1 |
  | ink on `#06080b` | 16.13:1 |
  | secondary text `#9aa3ae` on `#1c2735` | 5.91:1 |
  | red `#ff6a55` on `#1c2735` | 5.35:1 |
  | dark text on red | 7.11:1 |
  | border `#6b7788` on `#1c2735` | 3.32:1 |

- **Semantics:** the list entries are real buttons with `aria-pressed` and `aria-controls`; the charts have an `aria-label` and their contents are hidden from screen readers.
- **Script findings:** the two "hover without transition" findings are false alarms. The transitions are declared on the base rules (`index.css:102`, `:303`).
- **Tells (the clichés check):** the script found none.

**Problems:**
1. **Important:** the build was not run (no Node here).
2. **Nice-to-have:** the hairline under each list entry and above the facts row is on the allowed list, but that list was never approved, so it still counts.
3. **Nice-to-have:** the list notes are held in `src/sky.ts`, where the script doesn't read text. I read them by hand: they're factual and come from the data.

The Evening and Practical sections were both "heading left, content right"; I fixed that by making Practical read across in a row.

**Handed over, UNVERIFIED:**
- `npm run build` passes.
- Chrome DevTools Performance while moving the pointer: no frame over 16.7ms.
- The page at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440 wide: no horizontal scroll or clipped content, and the chart labels don't collide at 375.
- The OS reduce-motion setting on: the ring jumps.
